title: Dispatch: Assert literal canonical revokedPosition in the non-Dolt restore proof (review 5 evidence R4, liveness)
description:
Bounded test-only follow-up to eshyra-jhpt.rev12 (merged at f48dbfa). The non-Dolt test 'materializes campaign-rule reads without Dolt' in packages/core/test/checkpoint.restore.test.ts compares the restored DB's typed reads ONLY against the pre-checkpoint typed reads, both through the same rowToRule hydrator. Supervisor probe: changing rowToRule to return revokedPosition: null (while leaving the throw-guards intact) made NO test fail — both sides read null and deep-equal. So the assertion is not live against a symmetric hydration defect, which is exactly the class review #5118796759 R4 exists to catch.

WORKTREE / BRANCH: .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev13 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev13, cut from eshyra-jhpt at f48dbfa. npm ci already run.

THE FIX (test only; no production change):
1. In that test, additionally assert LITERAL expected values on the RESTORED db via getCampaignRule and listCampaignRules: the revoked rule has status 'revoked' and revokedPosition deep-equal to the canonical { sessionId: '__future__', turnId: '__future__', ordinal: <the ordinal the fixture revoked at> }; the superseded rule has supersededBy equal to its successor's identity and revokedPosition null; the active rules have revokedPosition null. Mirror the expectedRevokedPosition assertion the Dolt-gated block already uses.
2. Also assert on the restored db that the revoked rule is ACTIVE at the position immediately before the revocation ordinal and ABSENT at the revocation ordinal (listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition), as literal identity lists, not as equality with the pre-checkpoint list.
3. Keep the existing before/after deep-equals.

LIVENESS PROOF (required, report the exact observed message): temporarily change rowToRule in packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRuleStore.ts so the returned object carries `revokedPosition: null` while leaving the two throw-guards untouched; run the test; it MUST now fail on the literal assertion; then restore the production code (git checkout the file) before verification. Also confirm the test still passes unmodified.

VERIFICATION: npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing; report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution.
